note: Existing-source public educational gallery: CC photos and explicitly credited Bob Harms science/education-only photographs are distinguished. Source labels and arrows are not independent specimen voucher certification.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — SHEATH HAIRS, THEN BIGTOP
tiles.details: Bigtop lovegrass is a caespitose perennial with hardened bases, not a spreading annual. The 2005 Peterson & Valdés-Reyna treatment gives culms (30–)45–100 cm and broadly open panicles 25–85 × 15–40 cm; Kew/GrassBase gives 25–60 × 15–25 cm. Look at both lower and upper sheaths on the SAME rooted flowering plant: conspicuous hairs may occur across the sheath body as well as margins/apices. A purple, cloudlike panicle alone is not decisive.
tiles.short: Find hairs on several sheath BODIES and margins, plus a huge open panicle.

tiles.heading: 02 · TRUE INNER LIGULE VERSUS OUTER MOUTH HAIRS
tiles.details: Unfold the INNER blade–sheath junction at 10–20× beside a 1-mm scale. Peterson & Valdés-Reyna give ligules 0.2–0.4 mm, while conspicuous papillose-based sheath hairs can reach 6 mm. Do not label a tuft of outer sheath-mouth hairs as the true ligule. Current archived sheath closeups do not show a calibrated inner ligule, so add no anatomical ligule arrow.
tiles.short: True ligule ~0.2–0.4 mm, a short hair fringe; longer sheath-mouth hairs are NOT the ligule.

tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN PANICLE AND HAIRY PRIMARY AXIL
tiles.details: Kew describes an open ovate 25–60 × 15–25 cm panicle and bearded primary branch axils. The 2005 treatment describes a broader 25–85 × 15–40 cm head and notes axil hairs can vary. The Douglas Goldman archived photograph already shows a true hairy primary junction and attached spikelet, but no millimeter ruler. One hairy axil is supportive, not conclusive, because related lovegrasses overlap.
tiles.short: Follow the fine branches to a true primary branch insertion and look for the axillary beard.
tiles.status: AXIL IMAGE PRESENT — SAME-PLANT MEASURED AXIL GAP

tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE AND COUNT MATURE SPIKELETS
tiles.details: Measure 2–3 mature attached spikelets with a real 1-mm ruler. Peterson & Valdés-Reyna give 2–4(–5) × 1–1.5 mm spikelets with 2–4 florets; Kew/GrassBase gives 2–4 × 1–1.2 mm and 2–6 fertile florets. Count overlapping individual florets rather than branch tips. At maturity the rachilla may persist with paleas after lemmas fall. These are LITERATURE ranges, not measured lengths in current unscaled photos.
tiles.short: Tiny laterally compressed spikelets 2–4(–5) mm; 2–4 florets in 2005 treatment, 2–6 in Kew.

tiles.heading: 05 · GLUMES, LEMMA, AWNLESS TIP
tiles.details: Dissect the two basal glumes and mature fertile lemma at 20–40× with a 1-mm ruler. Peterson & Valdés-Reyna give lower glume 1.1–2 mm, upper glume 1.5–2.8 mm and lemma 1.6–2.4 mm. Kew gives narrower 1.4–2, 1.6–2.2 and 2–2.4 mm ranges respectively; glumes are one-veined and lemma three-veined. The lemma tip is acute but not long-awned. Existing whole-spikelet photos cannot support separate glume/lemma/vein arrows.
tiles.short: Lower glume 1.1–2 mm, upper 1.5–2.8 mm, lemma 1.6–2.4 mm (2005); awn 0 mm.
tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — DISSECTED GLUMES AND AWNLESS LEMMA

tiles.heading: 06 · TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES AND PUBLIC FINISH GATE
tiles.details: E. intermedia is often smoother across sheath bodies; E. trichodes may have conspicuous throat hairs rather than extensive sheath-body hairs; E. spectabilis also has an airy head. Do not decide from plume color or one hairy axil. NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: rooted same-plant Central Texas voucher, two lower/upper sheaths with scale, inner ligule at 10–20×, primary axil, 2–3 attached mature spikelets and glume/lemma/palea dissection at 20–40×. NEEDS_SITE_QA: check 7 image records, 9 comparison panels, existing arrows, source rights including CC BY versions, attribution, EXIF/GPS and mobile rendering. Preserve county nativity UNRESOLVED and native-metrics exclusion; not FINISHED.
tiles.short: Bigtop vs plains vs sand: compare sheath HAIR PLACEMENT, axils and measured florets.

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: BIGTOP LOVEGRASS: large open panicle, perennial tussock, but the much better first character is long HAIRS present over the leaf SHEATH BODY and margins (not only around the mouth). The actual source-image inspection shows those hairs on two sheaths. Lower panicle branch-axil tufts support ID when visible; missing in current macros. Compare with relatively smoother-sheathed plains and throat-hairy sand lovegrass; no cloudlike seedhead alone proves species.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: START WITH THE SHEATH: use stored Becky Dill photo to locate hairs on sheath body and sheath mouth. For E. hirsuta, Kew describes hirsute sheaths with hairy outer margins and oral hairs. Do not label every visible hair 'ligule'.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Bigtop lovegrass is a caespitose perennial with hardened bases, not a spreading annual. The 2005 Peterson & Valdés-Reyna treatment gives culms (30–)45–100 cm and broadly open panicles 25–85 × 15–40 cm; Kew/GrassBase gives 25–60 × 15–25 cm. Look at both lower and upper sheaths on the SAME rooted flowering plant: conspicuous hairs may occur across the sheath body as well as margins/apices. A purple, cloudlike panicle alone is not decisive.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Kew describes an open ovate 25–60 × 15–25 cm panicle and bearded primary branch axils. The 2005 treatment describes a broader 25–85 × 15–40 cm head and notes axil hairs can vary. The Douglas Goldman archived photograph already shows a true hairy primary junction and attached spikelet, but no millimeter ruler. One hairy axil is supportive, not conclusive, because related lovegrasses overlap.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Compared with E. intermedia and E. trichodes, examine several complete leaf sheaths: E. hirsuta has conspicuous hairs ON THE SHEATH SURFACE, not only concentrated at the sheath throat. Pair this with lower panicle axil beard and broad open panicle; E. spectabilis has a striking wide, often purple inflorescence but is not identified by color.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: TRUE SHEATH MOUTH · long dense hairs
panels.caption: Long pale hairs visibly arise along the margins and surface of the opened lower leaf sheath. The arrow points to the hairs themselves, not to a true ligule. Douglas Goldman, exact-source-labelled E. hirsuta, CC BY-SA 4.0; original JPEG unchanged. No ruler, ligule membrane, or hair-length measurement is visible.
